Heights and weights of children in the Berkeley Child Guidance Study

Source: R/data.R
BerkeleyGrowth.Rd

Longitudinal heights and weights of 66 boys and 70 girls from Berkeley, California, born in 1928-29, measured from birth to 21 years: at birth, 0.085 years, every three months up to 2 years, every year up to 8 years and every six months up to 21 years. Heights were measured from 1.75 years on; the heights of younger children are missing. The data were published as an appendix to Tuddenham and Snyder (1954). The heights of the first 18 years of most of the children are the growth data of the package fda.

Usage

BerkeleyGrowth

Format

A data frame with 4884 rows and 5 variables:

id

identifier of the child, a factor: 201-278 for the boys, 301-385 for the girls

sex

male or female

age

age in years

height

height in cm

weight

weight in kg

Source

The data set berkeley of the package sitar (version 1.5.0, licence GPL (>= 2)), with the transcription errors corrected there, without the other body measurements. The script that converts it is in the directory data-raw of the source package.

References

Tuddenham, R.D. and Snyder, M.M. (1954). Physical growth of California boys and girls from birth to eighteen years. University of California Publications in Child Development 1, 183-364.

Cole, T.J. (2025). sitar: Super Imposition by Translation and Rotation Growth Curve Analysis. R package, https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=sitar.

Examples

# the growth of the girls from 2 years on: the Preece-Baines curve, with the adult height b1 and
# the middle of puberty b2, and the peak height velocity of the pubertal growth spurt
girls <- subset(BerkeleyGrowth, sex == "female" & age >= 2)
fit <- gcTMB(height ~ age, data=girls, model="preecebaines")
coef(fit)
#> b1:(Intercept) b2:(Intercept) b3:(Intercept) b4:(Intercept) b5:(Intercept) 
#>    166.3370146     11.9345925    154.0119514      0.1180604      0.8819423 
#>      log_sigma 
#>      1.7673499 
maxrate(fit)
#> Time of the maximum growth rate (tmax), maximum growth rate (rate) and proportion of total growth at inflection (fraction):
#> 
#>          Estimate Std.Error
#> tmax       10.866   0.19993
#> rate        6.830   0.18381
#> fraction    0.883   0.00762
